Lifetimes of 5s5p3 5S°2 (39625.506) and 5s2 5p8s 1P°1 (57283.653): no measurement located.
Lotrian, Cariou, Guern, Johannin-Gilles (J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transfer, 1970s): measured Sn I transition probabilities - paper not located / not opened; no values taken.

Jiang, Wang, et al., "Experimental branching fractions, transition probabilities, and oscillator strengths in Sn I", J. Opt. Soc. Am. B 29, 1486 (2012): 66 measured branching fractions (mostly from even-parity 5pnp / 5pnf levels) - only the abstract could be opened (https://opg.optica.org/josab/abstract.cfm?uri=josab-29-6-1486), no values taken. Alonso-Medina, Spectrochim. Acta B 65, 158 (2010) (laser-induced plasma A values): not opened.

Measured branching fractions / A values for the 286.3, 300.9, 303.4, 317.5, 380.1 nm lines of the 5p6s levels: none opened; NIST values (Wiese & Martin 1980 compilation, accuracy D) remain the only ones in hand.
Precise absolute transition frequencies (frequency comb / calibrated wavemeter) for Sn I: none located.
Anselment et al., Phys. Rev. C 34, 1052 (1986) (286.3 nm isotope shifts and hyperfine structure of 18 Sn nuclei): abstract only, no numbers.
Measured g_J of 5p2 3P1, 3P2, 1D2 from atomic-beam magnetic resonance (Childs & Goodman): not in the abstracts opened; NIST Landé values are in the levels file.
Hyperfine constants of 5p6s 3P°2, 3P°0 (J=0, none) and of 5p5d levels: none located.
Xu, Feng, Sun, Dai, Chin. Phys. B 18, 3828 (2009): original not opened (abstract only); values taken second-hand from Zhang et al. 2010.
conflicts: 5p7s 3P°1 (48222.159 cm-1) lifetime: 20.4(6) ns (Zhang et al. 2010) vs 61(2) ns (Xu et al. 2009, same group, earlier); Zhang et al. argue the 2009 values were disturbed by cascade / collisional repopulation. Sum of NIST A values (Wiese & Martin 1980, accuracy D) would give 64 ns (derived).
5p5d 3F°3 (44576.006): 7.3(3) ns (Zhang 2010) vs 5.8(6) ns (Holmgren & Svanberg 1972, Hanle) vs 5.0 ns (Penkin & Slavenas 1963) vs 6.9(7) ns (Gorshkov & Verolainen 1985).

Measured lifetimes vs lifetimes implied by the NIST A values (1/sum A, derived; NIST accuracy D): 5p5d 3P°1 48981.934: 5.7(4) ns measured vs 50 ns; 5p7s 1P°1 52706.832: 14.6(3) vs 43 ns; 5p8s 3P°1 53020.952: 18.8(4) vs 71 ns; 5p7d 3D°1 55073.194: 292(9) vs 91 ns; 5p6s 1P°1 39257.053: 4.11(22) vs 3.05 ns; 5p5d 3F°2 43682.737: 23(2) vs 17.5 ns. The NIST sets are incomplete and of low accuracy for these levels.

5p6s 3P°1 hyperfine A: Yordanov et al. 2020 -4394(2), -4783(2), -5011(3) MHz (115, 117, 119) vs Baird et al. 1983 -4395.4(2.1), -4790.71(1.7), -5014.8(1.9) MHz; the 117Sn values differ by 7.7 MHz (about 3 sigma).

286.3 nm isotope shifts: Baird et al. 1983 (e.g. 124-112 = 1656.0 MHz) vs COLLAPS in Gustafsson et al. 2025 (124-112 = 1652.1(5.6)[7.1] MHz); consistent within the COLLAPS uncertainty, Baird is more precise.

Level labels: Zhang et al. 2010 list alternative term names for several 5p5d / 5p6d levels (Sansonetti & Martin vs Moore vs Dembczynski & Rebel); NIST calls 51113.059 cm-1 "5p7p 3P1" and 50756.212 "5p7p 3D1" while Zhang et al. 2008 (after Moore) use the opposite names. Levels were matched by energy and J.

Zhang et al. 2010 Table 1 attributes 6.5(1.0) ns for 47487.696 cm-1 to Andersen et al. and 4.5(5) ns for 44508.677 to both Holmgren & Svanberg and Andersen et al.; their Table 2 attributes 6.5(1) to Gorshkov & Verolainen and 4.5(5) to Andersen et al. The Holmgren & Svanberg abstract gives 3.9(5) ns for 5d 3D1.
notes: Isotope shifts are nu(first) - nu(second), kept relative to the reference isotope each source used (112Sn for Baird 1983 and the CRIS lines, 124Sn for the COLLAPS lines). For Gustafsson et al. "unc" is statistical and "unc_syst" systematic; only the stable isotopes 112-124 were transcribed (the table continues from 104Sn to 134Sn). 115Sn, 117Sn, 119Sn have I = 1/2, so there are no B constants; all A values are negative for 5p6s 3P°1 and 5p2 3P2/1D2 and positive for 5p2 3P1 (negative nuclear moments). Lifetime entries: Zhang et al. 2010 (time-resolved LIF, 38 odd levels 43682-56839 cm-1) for 5p5d, 5pns (n>=7), 5pnd; Holmgren & Svanberg 1972 (Hanle) for the three 5p6s levels - their paper was read only as the abstract on the Lund University portal; Zhang et al. 2008 for 5p7p (two-step excitation), which also gives Zeeman quantum-beat g_J factors. Older and conflicting values are under lifetime.alternatives. Zhang et al. print energies from Moore / Brown et al.; they were matched to the NIST energies by J and nearest energy (differences up to 0.6 cm-1 for the 5p7p levels, below 0.06 cm-1 otherwise). Ground-term (5p2) metastable lifetimes and linewidths are THEORY (Biémont et al. 1995 rates as tabulated by Zheng et al. 2026) and flagged as such. Extra fields beyond SCHEMA.md: ionization_limit, lifetime.alternatives, hyperfine.<A>.alternatives, isotope_shift_other, linewidth_Hz / linewidth_MHz, unc_syst, note. Level-wise comparison with NIST: the NIST Sn I A values are all from the Wiese & Martin 1980 compilation (tp_ref T4515, accuracy D except one C); measured lifetimes above should take precedence for total decay rates.
